newsitem.title: USA: Delta II rocket launch postponed for third time.
newsitem.headline: Delta II rocket launch postponed for third time.

text.p: A technical glitch Sunday forced the U.S. Air Force to postpone yet again the launch of a Delta II rocket carrying the first five satellites for the IRIDIUM LLC communications project.

McDonnell Douglas, makers of the rocket, said in a statement the launch was called off about four seconds before its planned liftoff of 8:01 a.m. PDT (1501 GMT). The liftoff was aborted when the launch conductor failed to get the correct indications on one of the rocket's ground support equipment items.

A spokeswoman at Vandenberg Air Force Base said a fourth attempt to launch the rocket had been tentatively scheduled for Monday morning at 7:55 a.m. PDT (14:55 GMT) with a five second window of opportunity.
This was the third time the launch had been postponed. Two previous two attempts, on Friday and Saturday, were called off due to high winds.
The planned launch in southern California is the first of a Delta II rocket since January, when a Delta II exploded shortly after takeoff from Cape Canaveral, Fla.

IRIDIUM is an international consortium of 17 companies, including Motorola Inc, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Raytheon Co, and Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co Ltd. The largest stakeholder is Motorola, with about 25 percent.
The consortium plans a global telecommunications network using 66 low-orbit satellites.
